senses: In Portland, Dorset, England, an outsider; somebody living on the island that wasn't born on the island.
ety: Comes from the days when sailors would stay on the isle of Portland, Dorset, England and visit the Kimberlin Club.

senses: Catachresis for kilowatt-hour.
An advocate or follower of structuralism.
examples: For a structuralist like Edmund Leach, the structure is the meaning. Genesis, for example, is about incest taboos; all the rest is noise and mystification.

senses: A period of adolescence for some members of the Amish that begins around the age of 14–16 and ends when a youth chooses baptism within the Amish church or instead leaves the community.
ety: Borrowed from Pennsylvania German rumspringe (“to jump around”). Compare German rumspringen.

senses: A private organization in New Orleans or elsewhere that exists to stage a Mardi Gras Ball, Mardi Gras Parade, or both.
ety: An intentionally archaic (or fanciful) spelling of crew, from the name of "The Mistick Krewe of Comus", the first such private organization.
examples: In 2004, as captain of the Rex krewe — one of the more progressive Mardi Gras organizations — Billy made a hesitant approach, too little and too late, trying to get to know Tootie Montana.

senses: The horn of an elk.
A highly-branched coral (Acropora palmata) supposed to resemble the horns of an elk.
Anyone or anything that intercepts something else.
A combat aircraft designed to intercept and destroy enemy aircraft before they can attack.
A guided missile designed to intercept and destroy enemy missiles.
An old French card game of Spanish origin, players attempting to make fifteen points.
Having branches; branching
examples: But it is chiefly in the interesting family Chalcídidæ that we find the greatest number of species having ramose antennæ.

senses: A person of two nationalities.
A Chaozhou-style raw fish salad.
An administrative subunit in Thailand below district (amphoe) and province (changwat).
ety: Borrowed from Thai ตำบล (dtam-bon).

senses: A fragrant plant in the rue family, Dictamnus albus.
False dittany (Pseudodictamnus mediterraneus, syn. Ballota pseudodictamnus)
A fragrant herb in the mint family native to the eastern United States (Cunila origanoides).
ety: From Old French ditan (French dictame), from Latin dictamnum, from Ancient Greek δίκταμνον (díktamnon), reportedly from Δίκτη (Díktē, “Dicte”), a mountain in Crete on whose slopes the plant grew.

senses: One of a set of wooden Russian dolls of different sizes, designed such that each fits inside the next.
ety: From Russian матрёшка (matrjóška), from personal name Матрёна (Matrjóna), formerly Матрона (Matrona), ultimately from Latin mātrōna (“matron”).

senses: A physician whose speciality is nephrology.
Of any evolving or learning entity, not well adapted for its environment.
A barbarian (variously used to refer to foreigners, Europeans, or pagans)
examples: We instructed our men to shoot first and inquire afterward, if a shenzi so much as showed himself in the clearing.

senses: A person engaged in a struggle.
ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀγωνιστής (agōnistḗs, “a contestant in the public games”), from ἀγών (agṓn, “contest, struggle”).

senses: The doctrine or policy of secession.
examples: Their History class made no mention of Biafran secessionism or any other subject related to the lives and times of black people.

senses: Having two refractive indices (depending on orientation)
The leaf of the oak.
A supporter of, or believer in, monarchy.
ety: From French monarchiste, equivalent to monarchy + -ist.

senses: The hereditary sovereign of Hyderabad, a former state of India.
ety: From Urdu نظام (nizām) and its source, Persian نظام (nezâm), short for نظام الملک (nezâm el-malek, “a ruler of the realm”).

senses: Synonym of sophistical, of or related to the ancient Sophists, characterized by fallacious reasoning.
ety: Learned borrowing from Latin sophisticus, borrowing of Ancient Greek σοφιστικός (sophistikós). Equivalent to sophist + -ic and sophism + -istic.

senses: The power of a sysop to block a user from participating in an online community.
ety: From ban + hammer, perhaps evoking a gavel.

senses: A pointed bullet.
ety: From German Spitz (“pointed”). Compare German Spitzgeschoss

senses: An arboretum, or part of an arboretum or garden, devoted to growing conifers.
examples: In the arrangement, of course, I should expect to see every hardy tree which could be collected in any part of the globe; and I even anticipate revelling in quercetums, fraxinetums, salicetums, pinetums, aceretums, &c.

senses: A thing, especially one seen as complex or having much associated with it.
A person who makes ceramics, such as pottery.
To identify the artist or the name of a song using the Shazam application.
ety: Apparently coined by American comic book writer Bill Parker in February 1940, from the first letters of Solomon, Hercules, Atlas, Zeus, Achilles and Mercury.

senses: A salad, from the Levant, made from toasted pitta bread with cucumber, tomato, mint etc.
The time when one takes a short sleep.
examples: Days filled with feeding, diaper changes, naptimes and bedtimes, trying to find a moment to go to the bathroom.

senses: A nonce word in Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky, explained by Humpty Dumpty as "four o'clock in the afternoon — the time when you begin broiling things for dinner."
The behavior of an adventurer; risk-taking.
The taking of excessive risks (by a government, etc) in political, economic or foreign affairs, often in disregard for established rules or norms.
A traditional short Portuguese unit of length usually about equal to 0.2 mm.
ety: From Portuguese ponto (“point”), Old Galician-Portuguese ponto, from Latin punctum, from pungō (“to prick, to puncture”). Doublet of point, pointe, puncto, punctum, punt, and punto.

senses: To make larger or more numerous.
To become larger or more numerous; to change to something larger, such as a house.
A slice of bread topped with sweet or savoury spreadable food such as butter, jam, honey, cream, or sauce.
A competitive examination, especially in medicine.
ety: From French concours. Doublet of concourse.

senses: Hazardous material(s).
A restaurant.
